title: Reprocessing steps and storage: awareness and limits
audience: Cleaning staff who help with reusable instruments, or who need to understand how they are reprocessed under a facility procedure.
learningOutcomes: State why cleaning comes before disinfection or sterilisation.
Describe the two methods of cleaning instruments and their protective equipment.
Explain the storage rule that keeps a reprocessed item at its level.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson explains the principles so you can spot poor practice and protect yourself and others. It does not authorise any cleaner to reprocess critical or semi-critical instruments. Reprocessing is carried out only by people the facility has trained and authorised, under its written procedure and the manufacturer's instructions. Medical equipment courses treat reprocessing as outside the external cleaning role.

instruction.heading: Clean first, always
instruction.body: Detergent-based cleaning lifts dirt and organic matter. It has to happen before high-level disinfection or sterilisation, since retained protein undermines both. Whatever remains after cleaning cannot be neutralised later. Start on instruments promptly after use, before residue sets, and disassemble detachable parts.

instruction.heading: Automated and manual cleaning
instruction.body: Ultrasonic baths and washer-disinfectors lower the amount of manual handling and suit robust basic instruments. Load hinged instruments open, stop items overlapping, and separate components when possible. Hand scrubbing is reserved for fragile instruments or sites without automation: brushing removes soil while fluid is forced through lumens. Required protection: a plastic apron, heavy gloves and a face shield, and no leaning into splashes or sharp tips.

instruction.heading: Disinfection and sterilisation
instruction.body: Disinfection inactivates most vegetative microbes via heat or chemicals, but falls short of sterility. Heat-resistant goods are generally steam-sterilised, whereas heat-sensitive goods need a low-temperature process. Validated sterilisation aims for a sterility assurance benchmark near one in a million (10 to the power minus six), and records prove each cycle ran.

instruction.heading: Storage keeps the level
instruction.body: Storage has to preserve each item's reprocessed status. Sealed sterile packs stay dry, clean and clear of sharp edges, and the wrap keeps out contamination while stored. Inspect surfaces regularly for cracks or breaks, and repair or discard any item that no longer works or cannot be reprocessed properly.

procedure: Confirm that the facility's written procedure authorises the task you are performing.
Put on the protective equipment the procedure names before handling the item.
Clean the item promptly after use, taking apart any pieces that separate.
Load an automated cleaner correctly, or clean manually with brush and fluid as the procedure directs.
Rinse residual cleaning agent off as the product requires, before disinfection.
Store the item in its designated, dry, protected location, and check that packaging is intact.

workedExamples.situation: A clinic cleaner is asked to 'quickly wipe the scissors' a nurse has just used, then put them back in the sterile pack.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop. Cleaning and sterilising are separate, authorised steps, and returning an item to a sterile pack without the authorised process breaks the storage rule. Refer the scissors to the nurse or the reprocessing team, and do not pack them.

equipmentAndPpe: Face guard: eye protection with a mask or a visor
Soft brush and detergent for manual cleaning, as the procedure states

commonErrors.error: Disinfecting an item before it has been cleaned.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean first. Leftover soil weakens disinfection and sterilisation.
Avoid stacking, open hinged items fully, and take items apart as far as possible.

commonErrors.error: Storing a sterile item in a damaged or wet wrap.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the wrap before storage, and treat any damaged or wet pack as not sterile.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Reprocessing is authorised only through the facility's written procedure and the manufacturer's instructions. This lesson is not that authority (licence notice).
Enzyme cleaners do not disinfect, and disinfectants can knock out their enzymes. Rinse the enzymes off fully, since leftover residue can provoke reactions.
Avoid splashes to the eyes and mouth, and injuries from sharp items, during manual cleaning. Use the protective equipment and treat every sharp as a hazard.

qualityStandard: Learner states the reason cleaning precedes disinfection.
Learner names the protective equipment for manual cleaning.
Learner identifies an item that is not in a valid storage condition.
documentationEvidence: Reprocessing log, where the facility requires one, showing method and operator
Storage check record for packaged items
summary: Clean before disinfecting or sterilising; leftover soil weakens both.
Automated and manual cleaning both depend on correct loading, protective equipment and rinsing.
Storage preserves the reprocessed level, and damaged packs are not used.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must an instrument be cleaned before it is disinfected or sterilised?
options: Because the disinfectant needs a wet surface to work at all and it works fastest on warm items
Because leftover protein or soil blunts the effect of disinfection and sterilisation.
Because the cleaning step is only for appearance and it is done after the packing
Because sterilisers cannot be switched on before lunch and the staff do not know how

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the guideline's rule about enzymatic cleaners?
options: They are disinfectants and can replace the disinfection step.
They do not disinfect, and residue left on the item can trigger reactions.
They should be left on the item for a week and then rinsed off with warm water
They are only for use on the outside of a patient and never on any instrument at all

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the storage requirement for a sterile packaged item?
options: It can sit in a damp cupboard among unrelated stock for a week
It is kept dry and clean, shielded from sharp items, with an unbroken wrap.
It should be left open to the air so it dries faster on the bench
It is kept in the pocket of the person who cleaned it until it is needed

sourceReferences: Australian Guidelines for Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare, B1.5.3 (cleaning), B1.5.4 (disinfection), B1.5.5 (sterilisation), B1.5.6 (storage and maintenance); B1.5.7 (further considerations); rights: not held by user; reworded (no copying)
